title: One Warhead Hits Chicago: What 800 Kilotons Does Street by Street
description:
Nine fifteen on a Tuesday morning. One missile leaves a submarine in the Atlantic, and eleven minutes later a single 800-kiloton warhead bursts over the Loop in Chicago. This is a street-by-street simulation of what one warhead does, ring by ring from the fireball (880 metres) to the last broken window (17 kilometres), and what the day after looks like.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. No crisis in it is real and no date is attached. The warhead size, the target, the launch point and the airburst are our choices, not a forecast; the blast, burn and fallout figures come from our scenario engine. Scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen; facts are labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the launch point, target, yield and burst type are ours, a scenario, not a forecast. We give no casualty figure for the simulated strike because no published study supports one.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble; thumbnail backgrounds are AI-generated. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
